questions.prompt: Describe the demands of officiating in a physical activity of your choice in terms of personal fitness, psychological readiness, personal attire and equipment.
questions.model: Activity: basketball. Personal fitness: a basketball referee must keep up with a fast-moving game for the whole contest, using speed, agility and endurance to stay in position to see fouls near the ball and the basket. Psychological readiness: the referee needs concentration for the whole game, composure when players or the crowd react to a decision, and resilience to put a mistake behind them quickly. Personal attire: a referee wears a uniform that is distinct from both teams, with footwear suited to the court surface, so the official is easily identified and has grip while moving. Equipment: a whistle, which must be clear and distinct, with a spare in case of failure, a timing device to keep the game time, and the signals or cards used to show decisions.

questions.prompt: Identify and explain two strategies an official can use to manage conflict between participants.
questions.model: First, separate the players early: the official moves between them and calls the captains to calm their team-mates, so the confrontation does not escalate. Second, use an advantage or a stoppage to cool the situation, then apply sanctions consistently, warning or cautioning the player who started the incident, and report any serious incident after the contest. Both strategies work because they reduce the chance of a fight and show that the official's decisions apply equally to every player.

questions.prompt: Outline two safety checks an official should make before a competition in a physical activity of your choice.
questions.model: Activity: soccer. First, equipment: the balls are correctly inflated, and the goals are secure with any padding on the posts in place. Second, facilities: the playing surface is checked for glass, holes and debris, the lines are clearly marked and the run-off areas are safe.
